name: Standing Calf Toe Raise

rehabilitation.clinical_protocol: NIH Senior Health & Physical Function Standards

steps: Stand tall facing a wall or the back of a sturdy chair with feet hip-width apart.
Place your fingertips lightly on the support surface for balance.
Slowly raise your heels off the floor, pressing evenly through the balls of both feet until you are standing high on your toes.
Pause at the top for one full second, feeling your calf muscles fully contract.
Slowly lower your heels back down to the floor under control.
coaching_cues: Push straight up through your big toes rather than rolling your weight to the outside edges of your feet.
Do not lean your upper body forward onto the support surface.
Maintain smooth, continuous movement on both the ascent and descent.

sources.attribution: NIH Lower Extremity Functional Strength Guidelines
